reply_text:
*Found 3 regressions; I’d hold the merge.*

1. *[P1] Feed pagination skips events sharing a timestamp* — `src/feed.js:11–13`
   Sorting still uses `(createdAt, id)`, but the pager and cursor now use only `createdAt`. With `a`, `b`, `c` all at timestamp 7 and limit 2, page one returns `c, b`; page two is empty, permanently skipping `a`.
   *Fix:* Use `[createdAt, id]` for both the pager key and encoded cursor.

2. *[P2] Existing feed cursors break after deployment* — `src/cursor.js:5–6`
   A cursor issued by `main`, such as `2:b`, now throws a `SyntaxError` in the base64url/JSON decoder. Clients continuing an existing pagination sequence cannot resume.
   *Fix:* Accept the legacy `timestamp:id` format alongside the new format during migration.

3. *[P2] String limits return oversized comment pages* — `src/pager.js:15–17`
   `commentsPage` passes its limit through unchanged, so `"2" + 1` becomes `"21"`. Reproduced with 10 comments: limit `"2"` returns 9 comments instead of 2, advancing the cursor past all nine.
   *Fix:* Normalize the limit to a number before lookahead arithmetic.

All 6 existing tests pass. `test/feed.test.js`’s “pages newest first” uses distinct timestamps; the timestamp-tie test in `test/pager.test.js` exercises comments only. Add regression tests for the three cases above.

Reviewed `pager-refactor` (`f6d44ec`) against `main` (`fe4d695`). No files changed.
